title: Disappointed, not sharp and angled enough
text:
Disappointed, not sharp and angled enough. When I found there was an actual implement for trimming wicks I was very interested. I had been using a pair of long pointed scissors, to some satisfaction but thought a wick trimmer would be great.

It was packaged nicely but the first time *and" probably last time I will use it was very disappointing. First thing I noticed is that the snipper part is not angled enough from the shanks to get into my jarred candles' wicks unless maybe they are at the very top, almost a new candle. I have to "dig" the points into the wax in order to get an angle to cut the wick. And even when I did bury the points into the wax the snipping part was obviously not sharp enough to cut a wick. I will stick with my scissors and maybe even a toenail clipper (not kidding). I don't have huge candles, maybe slightly smaller than the size of a quart size bell jar. But this trimmer is completely useless for the task. Maybe if you have huge diameter shallow jar candles it would work. The snipper is so dull though, I can't imagine it being any use. Let me get those toenail clippers out.
